note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: EU summit day 2 done, no cohesion headline; the Iran war's €100B+ fossil import bill is the euro's winter drag. France: Oct 20 revenue vote, Moody's Oct 23 (rejection motion failed 236–149). US: September federal budget balance Friday. No new US fiscal development.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: Split US surveys: Empire State +25.5 beat vs Philly 20.9 miss; retail +0.8% gasoline-driven (control +0.1%); claims 199K inline. UK GDP beat (+0.1%, 3m/3m +0.7%); Australia jobs -39.3K, unemp 4.7% (5-yr high); Japan machinery +5.2% beat vs IP -2.4% miss.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: PPI +1.3% m/m (vs 0.6%), y/y 6.3% (vs 5.5%); energy +10.8% (gasoline +20.3%); core +0.7% (vs 0.3%), y/y 5.0%. Two hot wholesale prints in two days — the market looked through both. France final CPI inline (HICP 3.4%, energy-driven); Swiss PPI missed (+0.3% vs 0.6%).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: October kept fading even as PPI ran hot (+1.3%, biggest since Mar 2022): LSEG ~29% (from ~31.6% morning, ~49% post-CPI); 10Y to ~5.05-5.10% (3-wk low). December ~90%+. ECB Oct ~12%/Dec live; BoJ Oct ~9%/Dec >80% (Koeda: neutral 'considerably above 1%'); BoE Nov ~86%+ (54/63 poll); RBA Nov questioned after the jobs miss; BoC ~25%; RBNZ two-way (Conway: 'most likely up'). Warsh 10:30pm CT — last before the blackout.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Verified COT (Oct 6 cut): DXY net +12,011 (modest); EUR shorts -99,332 (~1st pctile), AUD -98,588 (~2nd), GBP -97,611 — the squeeze risk sits in shorts, not dollar longs. Rule: stretched shorts = squeeze potential. Next COT Friday.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: AI risk-off: Nasdaq -1.05% (4th straight down day), semis 8th straight down, CoreWeave bonds >16%, VIX 2-wk high; defensive rotation (healthcare +2.6%, staples +1%). Haven ladder: gold +1.8%, CHF +0.59%, JPY +0.34% — the franc out-bid the yen; BTC -2.4%, no crypto haven.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: EIA confirmed the draw (-8.6M vs +0.2M fcst, 3% below 5-yr avg): Dec WTI +2.7% to $96.42, Dec Brent ~$106.10 flat — spread compressed to ~$9.7. Shadow-fleet easing talk leaked Brent's freight premium. Fresh Iran sanctions (designations, not relief). Gold ~$4,150-4,175 (+1.5%+) as the rate leg collapsed.
tot.title: Terms of trade
